title: Native formatter path
caption: How TSRX becomes marked legal TSX for one Oxfmt pass, then lifts back into formatted TSRX.

nodes.ordinary: Ordinary JavaScript and TypeScript call the OXC formatter directly.
nodes.tsrx: Formatting starts from the exact TSRX source bytes.
nodes.scan: A linear scan records the TSRX structure needed to project and later restore the file.
nodes.overlay: The compact overlay includes a source fingerprint so stale same-length structure cannot be reused.
nodes.projection: The formatter projection emits legal TSX with typed markers for TSRX controls, wrappers, dynamic names, and raw style payloads.
nodes.markers: One projected buffer uses collision-free identifiers so every scaffold occurrence can be validated and found once.
nodes.formatter: Canonical Oxfmt parses and formats the projected TSX exactly once.
nodes.arena: The formatter uses one arena-backed AST and does not reparse during the lift.
nodes.lift: One indexed forward pass removes proven scaffolding, restores authored TSRX syntax, and preserves source order and raw bytes.
nodes.formatted: The lifted output must contain no scaffold residue and must rescan to the same compact structural fingerprint.
